newsitem.title: UK: Uganda 1996/97 coffee crop may exceed 4.0 mln bags.
newsitem.headline: Uganda 1996/97 coffee crop may exceed 4.0 mln bags.

text.p: Uganda's coffee crop may exceed 4.0 million 60-kg bags in 1996/97 (Oct-Sept) given encouraging prospects for the mid-crop, a senior official said on Tuesday.
Uganda had recently revised down its 1996/97 crop estimate to 3.8 to 4.0 million bags from up to 4.4 million previously. In 1995/96, it produced around 4.2 million bags.
But William Naggaga, board secretary of the Uganda Coffee Development Authority, said the prospects for the June-August mid-crop were very good.
"We may exceed four million bags...that's the conservative estimate," he told Reuters at the International Coffee Organization (ICO) talks in London.
By April Uganda had produced 2.9 million bags, Naggaga said. That compared with 2.70 million bags in the same period a year ago.
Naggaga said a forecast for 1997/98 would not be available until July.
About 88 percent of Uganda's coffee is robusta. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
